## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Wǔmén chánjīng yàoyòng fǎ* (T619, one fascicle) is a Sarvāstivāda meditation manual originally compiled by [佛陀蜜多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%9C%9C%E5%A4%9A) (Buddhamitra) and translated into Chinese by [曇摩蜜多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%91%A9%E8%9C%9C%E5%A4%9A) (Dharmamitra, 356–442) under the Liú-Sòng. It systematizes the "Five Gates" (*wǔ mén*) of meditation — the five meditative antidotes corresponding to the five primary afflictions — that became canonical in East Asian *chán* practice.

**Abstract**

The *Wǔmén chánjīng yàoyòng fǎ* belongs to the cluster of Sarvāstivāda meditation manuals that entered China between the years of Kumārajīva and the mid-fifth century. The work is ascribed in the canonical bibliographies (*[Chū sānzàng jì jí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0084)*, *[Lìdài sānbǎo jì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011)*, *[Kāiyuán shìjiào lù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0093)*) to the Indian master [佛陀蜜多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%9C%9C%E5%A4%9A) (Buddhamitra) — a Kashmiri *yogācāra* teacher of obscure dates — as compiler, with the translation carried out in China by [曇摩蜜多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%91%A9%E8%9C%9C%E5%A4%9A) (356–442), who arrived in the south in 424 and was active there until his death. Date bracket follows Dharmamitra's productive period in Liú-Sòng (424–441). Like the contemporaneous T618, T619 is a Kashmiri Sarvāstivāda *yoga* compendium; it is closely related to a separate "Five Gates" tradition continued in T617's structure of paired remedies, and provided a model for later Chinese meditation manuals such as the *[Chánmìyào fǎ jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0250)*.
